title: Endgame Void (Faceless)

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY Endgame VOID Build In Auto Chess

body:
# Endgame Void (Faceless)

Void is a pure late-game scaling comp with one job: turn off every debuff in the
game. With the Void trait active your whole board is immune to stuns, silences,
hexes, disarms, and every other disable — the effects that normally decide
ultra-late-game fights. The trade-off is severe: Void is the *only* synergy you
may run. If any other race or class trait activates, Void switches off and your
board instantly becomes vulnerable, so the entire build is an exercise in
carefully *not* triggering synergies while fielding the strongest solo carriers
you can find.

## The one-synergy rule

Only Faceless Void needs to be on the board to enable the trait, but you must keep
every other synergy broken. In practice that means: exactly **two different
Demons** (so Demon stays off but you still get Doom), **at most two Assassins**
(Faceless Void already counts as one), and no doubled class or race anywhere.
Before adding any new unit, drop it on the board and check that no trait lights
up — one careless placement (a third Warrior, a Brewmaster next to spiders) turns
the whole team squishy.

## Core Units

The roster is whatever purple/legendary carries you can find that don't collide.

| Unit | Cost | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Faceless Void | 2 | Enables the trait — mandatory |
| Doom | 4 | Guaranteed Demon, disable + pure damage carry |
| Anti-Mage | 4 | Top damage dealer, mana burn |
| Medusa | 4 | Three-star stone gaze is the win condition |
| Monkey King | 4 | Repeated stuns |
| Sven | 5 | Cleave carry for the best items |
| Templar Assassin | 5 | Durable sustained damage |
| Chen | 4 | Revives fallen units at their star level |
| Zeus | 5 | Percentage-HP burst, lifesteal enabler |
| Gyrocopter | 5 | Flex physical damage |

Doom + a second Demon is the backbone; Anti-Mage quietly does the most damage even
at one star. A three-star Medusa is the real payoff — constant stone gaze from a
mana-fed Medusa carries the ultra-late fights.

## Items

Void has no defensive synergy, so items supply all the armour, resist, and
sustain.

- **Guardian Greaves** for team health + a disable cleanse.
- **Giants Ring** on Doom for the durable damage tank.
- **Battle Fury** or **Radiance** on Anti-Mage / Doom for cleave.
- **Refresher Orb** on Medusa so she double-casts stone gaze; pair with Dragon
  Lance for the mana-per-hit ramp.
- Skip Linkens Sphere — you're already immune to the disables it blocks; take
  armour or magic resist instead.

## Relics

- **Malefic Rapier** is the ideal economy relic — it snowballs the lose streak
  and the fast climb to level 9/10 the build depends on.
- **Stolen Gold / Stolen Vault** is the reliable default when nothing better
  appears; every bit of gold matters for a build that wants to sit at level 10.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Open the greediest lose streak you can — the guide even sells the starting Void on
round 3 to bank an extra interest breakpoint and hit 10 gold. Anchor it with two
Priests, hoard mangoes/tangoes, and prioritise gold and experience over units.
The board is genuinely weak until Faceless Void appears (often not until round
22), so accept the early bleed and lean on Chen revives and legendaries to
survive. Push to **level 9** before rolling in earnest, and only roll hard for
three-stars after **round 35**, when the extra IO drops make three-star purples
realistic. Never drop below ~25% HP without a mango banked.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Position like an anti-assassin board: keep squishy carriers off the front line
with melee bodies behind them to absorb the leap, and put Medusa central and
protected so her stone gaze reaches the most targets. Debuff immunity hard-counters
everything that relies on control — Savages, mind control, stun boards, mage
disables, disruptor silences. The dangerous matchups are the ones that ignore
debuffs entirely: **Assassins** (pure crit burst) and **Warriors** (out-tank and
reflect), plus **Goblins** with pure damage. Against assassins, master the
last-second board flip to dodge the smoke cloud, and win on positioning and
three-star density rather than trait immunity.
